walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Listening and Appraising — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Listening and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Listening and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: A quarter of its value

A double value

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: Music in 3/4 time.
It is the very first section.
It is the same as the chorus.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Music in 3/4 time.
Three different sections (ABC).
It is the very first section.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crotchet (quarter note)”?
options: Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quaver (eighth note)”?

sequence.def: Begins c.500: monks sing unaccompanied plainchant
c.1600-1750: harpsichord continuo and terraced dynamics
c.1750-1820: elegant balance; the piano replaces the harpsichord
c.1820-1900: rubato, chromatic harmony, huge orchestras
After 1900: serialism, minimalism and electronics arrive
